objective: Make the legacy boundary of workbench_virtual_mcu explicit in the artifacts rather than in one README sentence: label it legacy in the gate registries, point every consumer at the authority paragraph, and settle whether the parity claim is earned by comparing the transitions both implementations share.
decision_supported: Is workbench_virtual_mcu a safety reference or a test double, and does a green property gate say which?
acceptance: The mutation and property gate registries label the module legacy through MODULE_LABELS, so a green run cannot be quoted as firmware evidence without the label.
Every consumer of VirtualMcu carries a comment pointing at the authority paragraph in firmware/mcu/README.md.
A transition both implementations share is compared against the C source, so the word parity is either earned or dropped.

The comparison finds a real disagreement and records it as a finding rather than fixing it here: the C dispatch rejects STOP in MCU_STATE_FAULT with MCU_FAULT_STOP_REJECTED, while the stub accepts STOP from every state and lands in SAFE_STOP.
The module docstring states that it is a legacy stub and not safety evidence, names the C implementation as the authority, and records the disagreement.
The demo and the property suite pass unchanged: this issue adds labels and one comparison, not a behaviour change.
The README authority paragraph is unchanged.
commands: python3 -m ruff check tools/scripts/quality_gates.py tools/scripts/demo_scripted.py tests/property/ firmware/virtual_mcu/
python3 -m ruff format --check tools/scripts/quality_gates.py tools/scripts/demo_scripted.py tests/property/ firmware/virtual_mcu/
evidence: pytest tests/property/test_property_state_transitions.py: 7 passed, unchanged, which is the evidence that no behaviour moved.

The recorded disagreement, asserted from both sides: the C STOP case contains MCU_STATE_FAULT, MCU_RESULT_REJECTED and MCU_REASON_STOP_REJECTED; the stub accepts stop from FAULT and reaches SAFE_STOP.
The transitions that do agree, asserted from both sides: BEGIN_MOVE requires IDLE and enters EXECUTING; COMPLETE requires EXECUTING and enters IDLE; BEGIN_MOVE from EXECUTING is rejected by both.
ruff check and ruff format --check clean; make docs PASS.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The two implementations would have to be changed into parity; the issue says record the disagreement rather than fix it here, because the stub is not the reference.
The C implementation would have to be edited to match the stub; the C behaviour is the authority.

The freestanding target would have to be built and run to compare behaviour; the comparison reads the decision table from the source instead, because a Python test run has no ARM toolchain, and the test says so.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to firmware/mcu/core/**.
data_classification: Repository-local C, Python and Markdown. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and source reading; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: Labelling the module legacy could be read as retiring it. The label says what the evidence is worth, not that the double is useless: the demo and property suite still run through it, and MODULE_LABELS defaults every other module to authoritative.

Reading the C source instead of executing it means a semantic change that keeps the same shape would not be caught. The tests assert the guard, the target state and the rejection reason by name, so a changed decision fails even if the function names stay.

Recording the STOP-in-FAULT disagreement without fixing it leaves two behaviours in the tree. That is deliberate and stated: the stub is not the reference, so nothing downstream should rely on its behaviour, and a consumer that needs the C behaviour must use the C implementation.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: the module loses its docstring and the gates lose their labels. No behaviour changes either way.
